alignments.note: Waw takes And (rule 14).
Presentative וַיְהִי with its dummy subject and frame (rules 21, 45). The frame writes no complementizer here; the apodosis stands in the next verse.
Preposition takes at.
Assimilated article; the ASV writes that in the determiner slot and the demonstrative pronoun licenses it (rules 12, 41).
יוֹם rendered time.
Agreement article; one determiner is written and the demonstrative takes it (rules 41, 47).
Demonstrative pronoun takes that.

The waw opening the circumstantial clause takes the when the ASV writes for it (rules 14, 55). Competing reading: read when as a supplied subordinator and the waw as unrepresented, but a conjunction stands in the clause and rule 14 gives it whatever connective the ASV wrote.
Proper name.
Participial predicate with the construction-supplied copula (rule 20); down is the English phrasal particle of laid down and completes the lexeme (rule 44).
Preposition takes in.
Construct noun takes place; its determiner is the possessive, which the suffix licenses.
Suffix takes his (rule 18).
Waw rendered now, which rule 14's open list carries.
Noun takes eyes.
Suffix takes his.
Finite verb with its auxiliary (rule 17).

The adjectival complement takes the whole to wax dim, wax being the linking verb English writes where a copula would stand (rule 20) and to the marker its complement needs; head on the word carrying the lexeme (rules 31, 44).

The result subordinator so that answers to no morpheme: the clause לֹא יוּכַל is written asyndetically with no conjunction in it, so rule 55 marks the surplus and rule 2 keeps the two words as one unit, headed on the subordinating word. It is not the לְ of לִרְאוֹת: that preposition stands inside the clause, after its finite verb, and the ASV writes could not see with a modal's bare complement, which rule 52's closing sentence leaves unrendered. Competing reading: give so that to the לְ under rule 52's complementizer clause, set aside because that clause governs a לְ + infinitive the ASV recasts as the finite clause, and here יוּכַל is the written finite verb the subordinator stands over.
The ASV writes the negation and the modal as two words, so rule 2 splits them and the negative takes only its own not (rule 35).
יָכֹל takes the modal could with the subject pronoun rule 17 keeps on it.

The infinitive is rendered as the bare complement of the modal — could not see — so the ASV writes no word for this preposition and it keeps nothing (rules 52, 40), exactly as rule 52's cannot go beyond does.
Infinitive keeps the lexical verb.

review_notes: Corrected: the לְ of לִרְאוֹת was holding so that. Rule 52's closing sentence governs a modal's bare complement — could not see writes no infinitive marker — so the preposition is unrepresented under rule 40, and the supplied result subordinator is added under rule 55, the clause לֹא יוּכַל carrying no conjunction at all.
The variant unit WLC.1SA.3.2.v001 selected r00-base, which covers s014-s016; no fallback exclusion applies and rule 53 is not reached.
The frame's complementizer is not written in this verse; the ASV's when goes to the waw of וְעֵלִי, and the apodosis that stands in 1SA.3.4 (rule 45).
